title: Dottie's Herd Rescue
storyOpening: Morning mist curled across the valley as Dottie the young dinosaur lifted her head and heard a soft cry from behind a wall of ferns.
missionPrompt: A baby dinosaur wandered away from its herd. Follow the tracks, read the signs, and help Dottie bring the little one home!
readingPassage: Dottie pads carefully along a muddy trail where three-toed footprints press into the earth. Long ago, giant dinosaurs walked in valleys like this one. Some dinosaurs ate plants. Animals that eat plants are called herbivores. The crying sound leads Dottie to a baby triceratops hiding near a fallen log. Fossils are the left-behind parts of dinosaurs that scientists study today — but this baby is alive and needs help. Dottie nudges it gently toward the distant sounds of the herd.
storyEnding: The baby triceratops reunites with its herd. Dottie trumpets proudly — you helped a lost dinosaur find its family.
reflectionPrompt: What would you do next if you heard another dinosaur calling for help?
creativePrompt: Draw a picture of the valley where Dottie lives and label three places the herd might rest.
